Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

blame verb

also I don't blame you, reproach, to blame, I am to blame, I don’t blame you, put the blame on, push the blame on

classical

Traupman 148
Hor. S. 1.2.11: laudātur ab hīs, culpātur ab illīs (Lewis & Short)
Traupman 280

culpō, culpāre, culpāvī, culpātum

verb, first conjugation

to blame, reproach, find fault with

Lewis & Short: rare, mostly post-Augustan, and not in Cicero’s time (Horace, Ovid, Quintilian); Cicero says reprehendere or accūsāre.

Other words

  • reprehendō, reprehendere, reprehendī, reprehēnsum — blame, find fault with

    verb, third conjugation · also used · classical · Lewis & Short

  • culpa, culpae f. — blame, fault

    noun, first declension · also used · classical · Traupman 280

    “I am to blame” is in culpā sum; “put the blame on someone”, culpam in aliquem cōnferre (Traupman) or trānsferre.

  • incūsō, incūsāre, incūsāvī, incūsātum — accuse, find fault with, blame

    verb, first conjugation · also used · classical · Lewis & Short: classical, but not in Cicero; Traupman 280

Examples

  • Tē nōn culpō.

    I don’t blame you.Traupman 148

  • In culpā sum.

    I am to blame.Traupman 280

  • culpam in aliquem cōnferre

    to push the blame on someoneTraupman 280

See also attack, responsible, accept blame, criticism.
